translations.2879339180878659770: Every haul moves the cargo to the front o' one queue; when room be needed, the cargo at the back goes. Simple and predictable. A 60 GiB file downloaded once three days ago outlives a 2 MiB file downloaded fifty times four days ago, and someone tryin' a model once pushes useful cargo out.
translations.1914764339029037233: Like LRU, but how long cargo has sat idle be weighed against how long it takes to fetch again. A 30 GiB shard that took twenty minutes to arrive may sit idle longer than a config.json that comes back in a second. The cost be the measured duration o' the file's last fetch from the Hub; cargo stowed before this version be priced from its size with the estimates below.
translations.3416764453398626960: score = weight × ln(cost) − ln(idle time); the lowest score walks the plank first
translations.6608831776456866950: GreedyDual-Size-Frequency, the policy o' Squid and o' CDN caches. Cargo be worth frequency × cost ÷ size: a small file often downloaded be worth a lot per byte, a large shard downloaded once be worth little. Best hit rate counted in files, but large shards be sacrificed first; avoid it when those be exactly what costs bandwidth. Frequency fades with the half-life.
translations.739862626243855246: Every haul adds one to the cargo's counter, and the counter halves at every half-life. The lowest counter goes first. The HEAD requests clients send to check a file do not count. Size and cost be ignored, and cargo that was popular last month stays until the half-life has worn its counter down.
translations.3961640930617584275: A ring: cargo leaves in the order it came in, whether it was read again or not, so the hold turns over at a steady pace and nothin' sticks. Suited to an evaluation or CI buffer where each model serves a few days and never again; a file read every day be still fetched again at every turn.
